correctness.rationale: Reconstructed algebraic-closure proof from the 9896-byte Git RESULT.md. On the all-nonzero torus, e5=P sum X_i^{-1}, hence equality of hyperplane-constrained partials forces X_i^2 all equal; Frobenius injectivity yields the unique all-one point. Exactly one coordinate zero cannot satisfy e5=0, exactly two zeros give nonconstant partial gradient, and at least three zeros give the twenty singular lines, yielding 15 fourfold intersection points. At E, in X5=1 chart eliminate y4=sum_{0..3}y_i: exact f=e3(y0..y4)+product(y_i) of degrees 3 and 5 in F2. Since e3=sum y_i^3 under sum y=0, all projective cubic partials vanishing force all y_i equal, hence zero, so the tangent cubic is geometrically smooth. Strict-transform charts give C(z)+t^2Q(z), smooth along exceptional S; codimension-four ambient blowup discrepancy 3-3=0. Quadratic leading partials are a homogeneous regular sequence, yielding Hilbert series (1+t)^4, length 16; Euler identity in char2 ensures f belongs to the Jacobian ideal and Tjurina length remains 16. Dimension-one singular support implies geometric integral and Serre normality of the degree-five hypersurface. Independently verified the GF2 polynomial expansion, four leading gradients and 15 reduced rational boundary incidence points, not merely a saved VERIFY_OK. Residual boundary-line nonreduced Jacobian structure is not classified.
